messages:
Maria L.: Heads-up: EU customer reported a big p95 regression for v1/generate around 07:15 UTC. They saw TLS handshake spikes and intermittent 4xx timeouts.

Samir K.: Which regions? Is it isolated to one POP or continent-wide?

Maria L.: Customer says eu-west and eu-central affected; us-west/us-east appear normal. They attached a short curl + traceroute.

Maria L.: (paste)
```
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.eu/v1/generate
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.eu (54.92.12.101) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: Completed in 220 ms
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

Maria L.: Their logs show many entries like "TLS handshake 180-450ms" and some "connection reset by peer". Traceroute shows an odd hop: 120 ms on an internal hop which suggests cross-zone/POP routing.

Samir K.: That 120ms internal hop is a red flag. @netops any BGP flaps or route changes?

Liz H.: netops checking. No BGP anomalies in last 24h. I do see a spike in our edge TLS-handshake p95 in eu-central around 07:14 UTC. Some traffic is being routed to a secondary POP that proxies to a different cluster — longer path and likely cold TLS state.

Priya N.: What do we have for DNS TTLs? Could clients be pinned to a suboptimal IP?

Maria L.: LB short TTL = 60s, but enterprise proxies sometimes ignore that and cache A records longer. Customer is behind an enterprise proxy.

James P.: Also examine TLS session resumption rate. If that dropped, every request will pay the full handshake. I pulled metrics: session_resume_rate eu-* fell from 72% down to 18% during the window.

Priya N.: That explains it. If sessions aren't resuming, handshake latency spikes. Could be ticket/key rotation or nodes losing session tickets.

infra-bot: Alert: edge-tls-handshake-p95 > 200ms in eu-central at 07:14 UTC. Incident created #INC-20260214-89.

Maria L.: I gave the customer repro steps to help diagnose on their side:
1) curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.eu:443:54.92.12.101 https://api.redwood-inference.eu/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>"
2) tcpdump capture: `tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w tls-handshake.pcap`
3) traceroute -n api.redwood-inference.eu

Samir K.: I ran similar tests from our lab into eu-west and saw path churn: egress IPs alternating, which caused new TLS sessions to land on nodes without warmed ticket caches.

Liz H.: Hypothesis: anycast + origin routing + occasional proxying to a distant POP -> many connections land on nodes without session tickets, forcing full TLS1.3 handshakes. Also our ticket rotation may be too aggressive.

James P.: Quick mitigations we should consider:
- Reduce ticket key rotation frequency and add overlap window
- Tune gateway connection pooling and keepalives to reduce new connection rate
- Push short-term route preference adjustments to keep eu traffic inside same POP/AZ

Priya N.: I can push an alert: session_resume_rate < 40% triggers a paging so we catch this sooner.

Liz H.: I'll check edge route tables and health-probe sensitivity. If probes are marking nodes flapping, that could cause route churn. I can also push a temporary route weight adjustment to prefer closer POPs.

infra-bot: CI: edge-route-weight-update -> canary -> rollout started (job 8841).

Samir K.: Support should ask the customer to run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.eu:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.eu -tlsextdebug -status` and check for the TLS ticket extension and server-supported resumption.

Maria L.: Customer posted openssl output: "No session ticket extension" and Server Temp Key: X25519 on every connection.

James P.: That matches no resumption. Suspect ticket key rotation every 15m in eu as Priya mentioned earlier. That would break resumption for clients whose sessions straddle rotation windows.

Priya N.: I checked: our TLS ticket key rotation schedule in prod eu zones is 15m. Security allowed this historically but for edge we might need a longer window or overlap.

Samir K.: Proposed change: relax rotation to 2h and implement an overlap period where previous keys remain valid for N minutes. Need security signoff but seems reasonable to reduce latency impact.

Liz H.: I'll open a quick RFC and ping security in #eng-security. Meanwhile I'm rolling the route weight change to cut cross-zone hops; canary is already up on 2 POPs, monitoring handshake p95.

infra-bot: Canary update successful on 2 POPs. Monitoring handshake p95.

Maria L.: Support asked customer to retry after ~10m and re-run openssl. Customer reports handshake now 60-95ms and overall p95 down to ~110ms.

James P.: Nice. Routing tweak seems to have improved things. Action items:
- Liz: RFC for ticket rotation + overlap, audit edge health probe thresholds
- Priya: add alert & dashboard panel for session_resume_rate and handshake timings per POP
- Samir: draft KB for support with repro commands and mitigations (route preference, tcpdump, openssl)
- Maria: monitor with customer; close incident after 2h of stability

Liz H.: I'll also audit whether our upstream provider is doing frequent steering that causes microbursts across peering links. If so, we can coordinate with them.

Priya N.: Creating the alert now and will add to the Incident dashboard.

Maria L.: Customer said "thanks, noticeably better". I'll keep thread open until tomorrow.

infra-bot: Incident #INC-20260214-89 status updated: mitigated by Liz H.

James P.: Postmortem note: document enterprise proxy behavior (longer DNS caching) and recommend customers try our regional endpoints or DNS flush as a mitigation.

Maria L.: Agreed. Closing loop for now.
